title: Japan As We Saw It
publisher: Rand Avery Supply Company (for the author)
summary: A Boston man’s account of a four-month journey to Japan with his wife in the winter and spring of 1892, written as a practical guide for travellers “of moderate means” and drawn from his journal. They crossed Canada by rail and the Pacific on the steamer Empress of India to Yokohama, and went on to Kamakura, Hakone, Atami, Tokio, Nikko, Kioto, Osaka, Nara, Kobe, the islands of Awaji and Shikoku, the Inland Sea, Nagasaki, and the pottery towns of Arita and its neighbours, with a Japanese guide, Shimid. The book gives costs, hotels, inns, and manners, and describes visits, entertainments, and the damage of the earthquake of October 1891. Pronunciations of Japanese names are given in brackets throughout. It has more than eighty small engravings set into the text, and an appendix of money, measures, steamer fares, and a vocabulary of Japanese words and phrases.
